subject.title: Hard-delete or runtimeId migration needed for @apify/apify-openclaw-plugin

question: Should an authorized ClawHub operator apply the guarded runtime-ID repair to the live Apify package after verifying publisher control?
rationale: The mismatch and repair mechanism are established, but changing a production package's executable identity requires human authorization that this review cannot grant.

options.title: Apply guarded repair
options.body: Verify Apify control, review the dry-run, and apply the audited runtime-ID update, allowing the mutation to fail closed on any active collision.

options.title: Keep package blocked
options.body: Leave the record unchanged until publisher authority can be established to the operator's satisfaction.

options.title: Retire the package record
options.body: Use a destructive retirement path only if the identity-preserving repair cannot safely produce the intended state.

recommendation.title: Apply guarded repair
recommendation.body: Verify Apify control, review the dry-run, and apply the audited runtime-ID update, allowing the mutation to fail closed on any active collision.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced both relevant guarded operator repair paths and handled the analogous OpenViking case.
